ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and the regulations made thereunder; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 22; Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, as amended, including the ULC provisions and the significant-control information (SCI) record-keeping requirements applicable to Alberta corporations; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.); and FINTRAC policy guidance on beneficial ownership as an element of AML/CFT client due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of the passport or national identity document of every director and 25%+ ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin and the relevant passport-issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the document originates in a Convention state; otherwise Canadian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 30 days) for each director and relevant UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or financial institution, together with a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign-origin documents; no apostille required for Canadian documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of any corporate shareholder and its ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or company register in the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with a certified English translation if not issued in English or French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized corporate authorization (board resolution or power of attorney) appointing the Alberta registered agent and authorizing execution of the articles of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the foreign corporate shareholder or the appointed notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the document is issued outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owner or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal AML compliance file; notarized copy to be retained by Alberta counsel

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against: (i) the Canadian regulations made under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List, which is required for USD settlement and Apple/Google payment-rail payouts; (iv) the FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) framework covering foreign, domestic and international-organization PEPs and their family members and close associates; and (v) the Canadian banking-sector global financial crimes baseline. Screening must be completed before any funds are received and re-run at incorporation, upon change of control, and on a periodic risk-based cycle thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Access online portal operated by Service Alberta and administered under the Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or French characters; a foreign-language name must be transliterated into Latin script and supported by a certified translation or transliteration certificate. A ULC must include 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' or 'SRI' as its corporate designation. The name must be distinguishable from other Alberta and federal corporate names and must not be confusing with an existing NUANS record.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection may be contested by filing a formal name-reconsideration request with the Director of Partnerships and Corporations under the Alberta Corporate Registry. The request must include a fresh NUANS report, written submissions establishing distinctiveness, any consent letters from the relevant regulator, and, where confusion is alleged, evidence of first use and prior marks. The Director will issue a written review decision. An unsuccessful applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review within the applicable limitation period. Alternatively, the name may be resubmitted after removing the offending token or obtaining the required ministerial or regulatory approval.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Alberta permits a ULC to maintain a registered office at the physical street address of a licensed registered agent, but a purely postal or non-address virtual office is not acceptable for service of process. A virtual-office arrangement is low-risk for an EdTech language-learning company provided the address is a real, accessible physical location in Alberta, the agent can receive legal process, and the corporation maintains its minute book, significant-control register, share register and financial records at a disclosed location. For tax-residence and commercial-substance purposes, management and control should not be artificially displaced outside Alberta.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 3-6% annual probability. Registry officials may conduct unannounced inspections where there is a complaint concerning service of process, registered-office availability, unauthorized business address use, or a government/national-interest flag. The Canada Revenue Agency is more likely to conduct a document-based audit than a physical inspection, but records must be immediately producible.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c C-21, ss 6, 12, 21 and Part 9 (Unlimited Liability Companies, ss 89-108); Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, s 18 (unlimited liability share designation, where applicable); Income Tax Act (Canada), RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp), s 248(1) (definition of unlimited liability company).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta); filings effected through authorized Corporations Online service providers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation for an Unlimited Liability Company (Alberta Corporate Registry Form), accompanied by Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Alberta ULC; subscribers may record nominal consideration (e.g., CAD 1,000) in the Share Subscription List, receivable in a Canadian-dollar corporate bank account prior to share issuance; no escrow or statutory holdback is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the Share Subscription List presented to the Board, comprising 1,000 unlimited liability common shares subscribed by the initial Shareholders, is hereby approved, and the Corporate Secretary is directed to issue the said shares upon receipt of aggregate subscription consideration of CAD 1,000, without par value; (2) the registered office and corporate records office established at [●], Alberta, is adopted, and Practica Corporate Services Ltd. is appointed as registered agent; (3) the following officers are appointed: [Name 1] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name 2] as Chief Technology Officer, and [Name 3] as Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until removed by the Board; (4) the corporate by-laws, banking resolutions and electronic-signature procedures are adopted; and (5) management is authorized to execute all ancillary statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via Corporations Online or authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request, selecting a distinctive name with the mandatory legal element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'; if the name is cleared, reserve it for up to 90 days before formal incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Request Form
Name concept sheet with proposed legal element
Consent letter from the entity whose name concept is adopted (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report flags a confusingly similar name, file a revised Name Search Request with a new proposed name or submit a written reconsideration letter to the Corporate Registry within 30 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel and notary public; Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation containing the ULC share-class structure, designation of unlimited liability, restriction on share transfers if required, first directors, and registered office address; each subscriber and each proposed director executes the articles and consent forms, with signatures witnessed and notarized where requested by the Registry.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation for an Unlimited Liability Company
Consent to Act as Director (Form 25 equivalent)
Notice of Registered Office and Records Address
Notice of Directors
Notarized subscriber signature pages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Notice of Defective Filing, execute a corrective affidavit and re-file the corrected articles within the cure period (30 days) to avoid loss of the filing priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Registry and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporations Online) - Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation and statutory forms through an authorized Corporations Online service provider; pay the CAD 110 statutory fee (CAD 100 incorporation fee plus CAD 10 name search fee) by credit card; the Registry assigns a Corporate Access Number and issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the Companies Act (Alberta).
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation
Notice of Registered Office and Records Address
Notices of Directors and Director Consents
Payment receipt for statutory filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for non-compliance, resubmit a corrected package with the Registry's deficiency letter attached; pre-filing legal review is recommended because the incorporation fee is non-refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of By-laws and Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Alberta ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting; adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution approving the share subscription list, appointing officers, and establishing the registered office; adopt By-law No. 1; approve the minute book, corporate seal, banking resolutions, and share certificate forms; issue share certificates upon receipt of subscription funds.
required_dossiers: Minute book
By-law No. 1 (general corporate by-law)
Pro-Forma First Board Resolution (minutes)
Share subscription list and share certificates
Bank account opening resolution and signatory authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a board action is challenged for lack of quorum or defective notice, cure by executing a unanimous written resolution signed by all directors in lieu of the meeting pursuant to the Companies Act (Alberta).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Registration and Business Number (BN) Set-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, register the ULC with the CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain the nine-digit Business Number and program accounts: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll), and RD (director identification, if applicable); retain the legal name and registered office address exactly as filed with Alberta.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Alberta Corporate Access Number
Registered office address and director particulars
Shareholders' agreement if adopted
Bank account details for remittance links if desired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registered office (e.g., mail-forwarding address only), update the registered office address with the Alberta Corporate Registry and resubmit the BRO registration with the Registry's confirmation letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Filing and EdTech Payment-Rails Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Apple App Store Connect; Google Play Console
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporated entity's annual return with Alberta Corporate Registry within 15 months of incorporation; file the Initial Return (Corporation Information Return) with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) within 75 days of incorporation; then enroll the ULC in Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console as the merchant/developer of record, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, banking verification, and PIPEDA-compliant privacy policy.
required_dossiers: Annual Return (Alberta Corporate Registry)
ISED Corporation Information Return
Apple Developer Program Application and bank statement
Google Play Console Entity Verification pack
Privacy policy and terms of service for the EdTech application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment-rail verification is rejected due to entity-name mismatch, obtain a Registry Certificate of Status and re-submit; answer Apple/Google questionnaires within their appeal window to unlock the developer account.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no manufacturing or physical processing trigger; the authority of reference would be Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade (Industrial Licensing Branch) for a compliance exemption letter if requested.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required - statutory business licence exemption applies to pure software subscription services; a voluntary municipal business licence (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Licence) is recommended if a physical office lease is opened.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - service-sector software activity falls outside the mandatory and exempt activities list of the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation, Alta Reg 110/2013; no registration or full EIA report trigger.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC discharge; the only relevant standards are indoor IT equipment heat management (below 1 MW aggregate), compliance with the Designated Material Recycling and Handling Regulation for e-waste, and adherence to municipal solid-waste bylaws for IT hardware disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety or structural inspection is triggered for a virtual headquarters; if the ULC occupies a physical office, Alberta Fire Code (Alta Reg 55/2019) inspection and municipal occupancy permit apply, and workers' compensation coverage registration with WCB-Alberta is mandatory upon hiring employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; digital portals: Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account (MyBA), GST/HST NETFILE, T2 Corporation Internet Filing. Provincial corporate registry: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Online Service) under Service Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the ULC under Part 5.1 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (Alberta ULC regime effective 2021) and obtain the Alberta Certificate of Incorporation. Step 2: Register with the CRA for a Business Number (BN) via BRO or Form RC1, electing the Corporation Income Tax account and the GST/HST account (and Import/Export account only if tangible goods are eventually exported). Step 3: The BN is issued instantly online; the GST/HST account becomes effective as of the quarter in which worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold, with mandatory registration within 30 days thereafter. Step 4: Non-resident (e.g., U.S.) shareholders must deliver Form W-8BEN-E and a valid U.S. TIN; the ULC should retain the Article XXIX(8) treaty election documentation for the fiscally transparent election file. Step 5: File annual T2 corporate returns and periodic GST/HST returns electronically via CRA's MyBA portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Alberta ULC is a 'taxable Canadian corporation' for Canadian income tax purposes, but is uniquely eligible under Article XXIX(8) of the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention (Fifth Protocol) to elect fiscally transparent (partnership/disregarded entity) treatment for U.S. tax purposes; U.S. shareholders may file Form 8832 (Check-the-Box) to effect the U.S. classification. For GST/HST, the ULC may execute a joint election under Excise Tax Act s. 156 with an affiliated corporation to treat inter-corporate supplies as made for nil consideration. Alberta does not provide a separate entity-classification check-the-box regime; provincial corporate income tax follows federal entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax); Alberta levies no Provincial Sales Tax and no HST applies in Alberta
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in aggregate worldwide taxable supplies in any single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold, Excise Tax Act s. 148); once exceeded, mandatory GST/HST registration within 30 days
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping requirement. The CRA administers the voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (Peppol band); GST/HST returns and T2 returns must be filed electronically by most registrants, with mandatory electronic filing for GST/HST registrants whose annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,000,000 and for corporations whose gross revenue exceeds CAD 1,000,000. Invoices may be issued electronically (PDF/XML) without government pre-approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of subscription-based digital language-learning software and automated tutoring services to non-resident persons are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI, Excise Tax Act: s. 7 (supply of services to a non-resident otherwise than in Canada in respect of real property in Canada or tangible personal property in Canada) and s. 10 (supply of intangible personal property to a non-resident not for use in Canada). Where sales are made through Apple App Store (Apple_IAP) or Google Play Billing, the digital economy marketplace rules (effective July 1, 2021) deem the non-resident platform operator to be the supplier of the underlying subscription to Canadian consumers, so the ULC's platform-originated revenue stream is not subject to GST/HST collection by the ULC; a supply from the ULC to the non-resident platform operator may itself be zero-rated as a service/intangible supplied to a non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) - required only if physical educational goods are exported; not required for pure digital subscription services
Commercial invoice / order record identifying the non-resident customer and the digital subscription delivered
Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console financial reports showing country-level sales, payment settlement amounts, and any platform-remitted GST/HST
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT records evidencing receipt of foreign funds
Non-resident customer attestation or IP geolocation / subscriber onboarding logs establishing non-residency (B2B: signed NRA self-declaration)
GST/HST return and zero-rated supply worksheet demonstrating the export classification of the relevant revenue
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess retroactively for four years under Excise Tax Act s. 298(1); the limitation period is unlimited where a return contains misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud (ETA s. 298(6)). Fraudulent zero-rating exposes the registrant to a civil penalty under ETA s. 280.1(1) equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the net tax sought to be evaded, plus interest and retroactive clawback of input tax credits and refunds. Income tax gross-negligence penalties (ITA s. 163(2)) of 50% of the understated tax may also apply. Criminal prosecution for tax fraud exceeding CAD 1,000,000 under Criminal Code s. 380(1)(a) carries a maximum penalty of 14 years' imprisonment, fines at the court's discretion, and CRA collection measures including refund set-off, bank freezing, and asset garnishment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada maintains a liberalized, fully floating foreign-exchange regime; there is no dedicated FX exchange-control authority. FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) is the financial intelligence unit responsible for AML/ATF reporting and large cross-border transaction surveillance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current account and capital account items. No quantitative restrictions, licensing, or prior approval requirements apply to CAD conversion, foreign-currency holding, or cross-border capital movements. Profit repatriation from a Canadian ULC to non-resident members is unrestricted under exchange-control law but is subject to Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, potentially reduced under an applicable income tax treaty). EdTech subscription revenue constitutes an export of digital services that is zero-rated for GST/HST purposes; no services-sector foreign-ownership restriction applies. The ULC may freely maintain CAD and USD operating accounts and settle contractual obligations in either currency at market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada does not impose surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timelines on export proceeds received in foreign currency. An Alberta ULC may retain USD or other foreign currency indefinitely in domestic or offshore accounts. However, FINTRAC reporting obligations apply to (i) electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more entering or leaving Canada, and (ii) physical cross-border currency movements above the same threshold. The corporate group must also file Form T1135 (Foreign Income Verification Statement) if the ULC holds specified foreign property with an aggregate cost amount exceeding CAD 100,000.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD and USD dual-currency treasury sweep)
Operational Account (cross-border wire concentration with TD Bank US affiliate)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (subscription/settlement routing for app-store proceeds)
Operational Account (foreign-currency ancillary account via CIBC Global Money)
Operational Account (USD concentration and commercial FX derivatives line)
Operational Account (Alberta provincial Crown bank, secondary local-clearing account)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a supporting disbursement rail only, not as the primary treasury. Wise (Wise Canada Inc.), Payoneer, and Airwallex are FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses (MSBs) operating through partner chartered banks; they are not Schedule I banks, are not CDIC members, and their balances do not carry deposit insurance. Legally they may open CAD/USD virtual accounts for the ULC and provide local clearing in foreign markets (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP), but the core capital-escrow and liquidity-settlement function must remain at a Canadian chartered bank to satisfy the underwriters and corporate-governance expectations of the ULC. Use case: contractor payroll in emerging markets and optimization of Apple/Google payout receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian AML/ATF law permits remote video identification under FINTRAC guidelines, but Tier 1 chartered banks in practice require one in-person account-signatory interview, normally with the founding or financial director. A Calgary or Edmonton branch meeting with the designated director (plus notarized identification for all other directors) provides the fastest onboarding. Pure remote onboarding is legally available but typically triggers enhanced compliance review for an unlimited-liability entity and may require certified copies of passports, corporate registry extracts, and a legal opinion addressing director exposure. Recommended route: one executive attends a physical KYC interview; remaining directors complete video verification using a licensed verification agent, followed by notarized corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC unlimited-liability structuring — bank underwriting flag on director/shareholder personal exposure and unlimited liability of the corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; Articles of Incorporation with the ULC election; executed Unanimous Shareholder Agreement; board resolution authorizing the account; notarized directors' identity and proof-of-address package; audited or reviewed financial statements or an opening balance-sheet statement; a legal memorandum describing the limited-purpose operating scope of the ULC and the contractual capping of liability in EdTech subscription agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership transparency — failure to identify individuals with significant control (ISC) triggers elevated FINTRAC reporting and potential denial of service.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta registry extract of the Individuals with Significant Control register; organizational chart tracing each direct and indirect member of the ULC; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for all capital contributors; signed CRS/FATCA self-certifications for each non-resident member; declaration confirming no bearer shares and no nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS/EdTech revenue flows intermediated by Apple App Store and Google Play — bank concern over unverifiable digital-service trade and app-store refund/chargeback volume.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program and Google Play Developer agreements; monthly Apple/Google payout statements; GST/HST registration certificate and evidence supporting zero-rated digital-export treatment; transaction-level subscription ledger and reconciliation files; FINTRAC-compliant large-transaction reporting trail; public-facing terms of service and refund policy to evidence chargeback predictability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder capital injection from an offshore parent into the ULC — suspicion of round-tripping or unsubstantiated loan/equity classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed share-subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement at arm's-length terms; bank statement evidencing the wire trace; board minutes recording the capital decision; CRS/FATCA declarations; transfer-pricing memorandum and interest-rate benchmarking for any shareholder loan to mitigate deemed-interest or withholding issues; confirmation that no statutory minimum paid-in capital applies and that the injection is recorded in the Alberta corporate records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing of equity or shareholder-loan capital from a non-resident parent: SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire for USD) directed to the ULC's account at its Canadian Schedule I bank, with remittance field 70 stating 'Share Capital Injection — CA_ULC EdTech' and referencing the subscription or loan agreement. CAD-denominated high-value settlements clear in real time via Lynx (Payments Canada); USD receipts clear via CHIPS/Fedwire through the Canadian bank's US correspondent. The receiving bank requires a corporate resolution, executed equity/loan documents, CRS/FATCA self-certification, and confirmation of any Investment Canada Act filing status (limited to sectors subject to review; digital EdTech generally falls below the WTO review threshold). FINTRAC reporting applies where the transfer exceeds CAD 10,000. Funds are freely convertible to CAD at spot and may be swept into an interest-bearing treasury account until deployed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for international vendor payments, contractor disbursements, and app-store royalty/profit-share remittances; field 70 must reference the underlying invoice or settlement statement. Apple and Google payout proceeds are received in USD through the operational account and may be netted against USD disbursements to reduce conversion costs. For large platform subcontracting relationships, an standby letter of credit or demand guarantee issued by the Canadian bank may be used as a performance bond; documentary commercial letters of credit are not standard for purely digital EdTech services and are reserved for physical goods resale arrangements. Domestic CAD vendor payroll and operational expenses clear via Payments Canada ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System) or same-day Lynx for high-value items. All intra-group disbursements must be supported by intercompany agreements and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) with tenors up to 24 months executed under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Canadian bank dealing desks
European-style OTC FX options (call/put with premium) and zero-cost collars on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, permissible for hedging app-store USD revenue volatility
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps aligning USD-denominated receipts with USD-denominated disbursement obligations

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for exotic or restricted currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, ARS) where deliverability is constrained; NDFs are unnecessary for the freely convertible CAD market
Natural hedging via dual-currency USD/CAD treasury accounts and matching cash-flow buckets to reduce synthetic derivative reliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Alberta Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or the date of the last annual return, whichever is later
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Notice of default may be issued; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution. Reinstatement requires payment of outstanding fees and may require court order or registrant restoration process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; additional penalties for repeat failures; gross negligence penalties may apply; director liability may arise for assessed penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based threshold under Alberta law. An auditor must be appointed each fiscal year unless a unanimous shareholder resolution waives the audit. An audit is mandatory for reporting issuers, corporations subject to specific statutory requirements, or if the waiver is not passed by all shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may elect ASPE (Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) or IFRS consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta requires an ongoing register of individuals with significant control (ISC) under the ABCA. The ISC register is not filed annually with the Alberta Corporate Registry; it is maintained at the registered office and must be updated within 15 days of any relevant change. An annual board review and confirmation of the ISC register is recommended before filing the annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 - $550 for a registered agent and office service; lower if self-managed
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 - $15,000 for a compact audit; waived if unanimous shareholder resolution is in place

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate (after 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction) plus 8% Alberta general corporate rate = 23% combined headline rate for a non-CCPC ULC.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory federal or Alberta tax holidays. Federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit: 35% refundable for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs), otherwise 15% non-refundable for a non-CCPC. Alberta Innovation Employment Grant provides up to 20% of eligible incremental payroll costs for technology companies within prescribed caps. Software subscription revenue is not eligible for the manufacturing and processing deduction. A ULC remains a taxable Canadian corporation for Canadian income tax purposes even if treated as a pass-through entity for US check-the-box purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (single integrated federal and Alberta filing); electronically submitted through CRA-approved EFILE or CRA XML API.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one T2 per taxation year. Monthly or quarterly Part I tax instalments may be required for corporations with high tax payable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than 6 months after the ULC's fiscal year-end. Final tax balance due is 2 months after year-end for a non-CCPC (default for a ULC controlled by non-residents), or 3 months after year-end for a qualifying CCPC. No extension is available for late filing unless a CRA waiver on corporate dissolution or unreasonable hardship is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All EdTech subscription fees, one-time software licences, automated tutoring service fees, and ancillary content revenue recognized under IFRS or ASPE; include Apple/Google IAP settlements gross less app store commissions, taxes and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Canadian-resident ULC, report world revenue in Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada annual average exchange rate. Non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation for this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less cost of goods sold, software R&D wages, marketing, overhead, capital cost allowance, and amortization; add taxable capital gains; subtract available non-capital loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply CRA exchange rates for all foreign-currency transactions. Non-resident treaty considerations do not attach to this line; they affect only withholding tax on subsequent profit repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax computed at the basic 28% rate less 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction, yielding 15% for general business income; add Part I.3 minimum tax when applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A ULC controlled by non-residents is not eligible for the small business deduction; the general corporate rate applies. A special election as a 'non-resident-owned investment corporation' is not advisable and is rarely available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial corporate tax allocation: taxable income allocated to Alberta based on permanent establishment factors (gross revenue, wages and salaries, and fixed-place-of-business assets in Alberta vs. elsewhere).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an Alberta-incorporated ULC, the corporation is presumed to have a permanent establishment in Alberta; a nil allocation is only valid if no office or staff is present and the corporation merely exists on paper.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months (maximum 17%). Repeat late filing is penalized at a higher first-bracket rate. Interest accrues daily at the CRA prescribed rate (currently 9% per annum). If the T2 is filed more than 6 months after the deadline and tax remains unpaid, CRA may impose a gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder. Under the Canada–US DTA, reduced to 5% for a US recipient corporation that owns at least 10% of the ULC's voting shares and 15% for a US individual receiving dividend income. Treaty reductions under Canada-UK and Canada-Netherlands DTAs may also apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident payee must complete and deliver to the Canadian payer the applicable CRA declaration form: NR301 (individual) or NR302 (corporation), and provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. The payer applies the reduced treaty rate at source. If the full 25% has already been withheld, the beneficial owner must file a refund application under subsection 227(6) of the Income Tax Act no later than two years after the calendar year of payment. CRA may require annual proof of active business presence under the Canada-US DTA Limitation on Benefits clause (Article XXIX A) and may reject the claim where the ULC lacks economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding rates: interest 25%; royalty 25%. Under the Canada-US DTA, arm's length interest paid to a US beneficial owner is generally exempt from Canadian withholding tax (0%) unless the interest is participating or tied to profits. Royalties from patents, trademarks, and know-how are generally taxed at 10%. Payments for certain computer software copyrights may be characterized as business income (0%) rather than royalties when the payment is made for a copy for internal use and does not confer rights of public reproduction or distribution.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CRA administrative contemporaneous documentation threshold: CAD 1,000,000 for non-arm's length transactions with a non-resident related party (aggregated by transaction category). Loan and financing transactions are documented from CAD 500,000. A complete Local File / Master File becomes mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CAD 1,500,000,000 (CDN equivalent of €750M) under the Country-by-Country Reporting rules. Documentation must be produced and provided to CRA within 30 days of written demand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose a standalone Economic Substances Regulation regime analogous to offshore jurisdictions, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245 of the Income Tax Act) and the Canada-US DTA Limitation on Benefits Article XXIX A require demonstrable business substance. A ULC must hold active employees, business premises, material capital at risk, and actual management decision-making in Canada to sustain treaty benefits and to avoid GAAR reassessment. CRA may disregard the separate legal personality of a shell ULC and allocate all income to the controlling shareholder where the corporation is a mere conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting gross subscription revenue from Apple/Google settlement statements, fabricating SR&ED hours, or offshoring IP without a valid arm's length licence arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239(1): on summary conviction, a fine between 50% and 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 2 years; on indictment, a fine between 100% and 200% and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) of 50% of the understated tax, plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed, participated in, or acquiesced in the fraud are personally liable under criminal law, face fine and imprisonment, and may be subject to a travel ban under s.242(2) of the Income Tax Act. The corporate veil is pierced where the ULC is used as an alter ego; directors may be ordered to make personal restitution and disgorgement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and provide contemporaneous Local File/Master File documents within 30 days of a CRA request for non-arm's length transactions, or pricing intercompany software royalties below arm's length to artificially reduce Canadian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.247(3) penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment, plus reassessment of omitted taxable income and daily interest. The penalty is not relievable where the taxpayer has not made reasonable efforts in documentation. Negative adjustments are prohibited for taxpayers that fail to provide adequate documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for withheld payroll/GST under s.227.1, but for pure transfer-pricing reassessment the liability remains at the corporate level. A director who knowingly enters into a pricing arrangement that strips profits without business rationale may be personally charged under criminal fraud provisions and may be subjected to travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the ULC as a mailbox with no employees, no office, no bank account, and no decision-making in Alberta, while using the entity solely to extract dividend or royalty flows to a zero-tax jurisdiction or to claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment under s.245 nullifying the entire tax benefit; denial of treaty benefits under Article XXIX A LOB; 50% gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2); additional interest charges. In flagrant cases, the CRA may apply s.18(4) thin-capitalization rules to deny interest deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate conduit arrangements may be held personally liable for the resulting tax benefit; Canadian courts may lift the corporate veil and impose personal ownership of the ULC's income. A lifelong travel ban and seizure of personal assets are possible in fraudulent versions of the same scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the EdTech platform to aggregate Apple/Google payouts, convert foreign currency for users, or move settlement funds to unrelated parties without registration as a Money Service Business under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PCMLTFA s.82: failure to register is a summary offence with corporate fines up to CAD 1 million. FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 1 million per contravention. Where the payment rail is only Apple/Google IAP and the ULC does not interact with end users' funds, MSB registration is not required; any conversion of funds for a third party triggers registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s.75 PCMLTFA, directors and officers are personally liable for the corporation's contravention if they knew or ought to have known of the matter and failed to exercise due care. If the unreported flows form part of a money laundering offense, directors face imprisonment and confiscation orders.
